tokenColors.name: Keyword that TextMate files under control but VS does not
HTML attribute (VS colours it apart from XML)
XML text between tags (also XAML and MSBuild files, which VS draws as XML)
XML: = inside a tag is a delimiter in VS (the grammar gives it no scope of its own)
XML attribute quotes (VS colours them apart from the value)
XML entity reference (attribute colour in VS, whole &name;)
XML DOCTYPE keywords take the element colour, the names in them the attribute colour
YAML key (keyword blue in VS, like its numbers)
YAML anchor name (keyword blue in VS; the & stays plain)
YAML alias and block-scalar indicators stay plain in VS
VB: As and primitive types are keywords in VS (the ASP grammar scopes them as operator and type)
PowerShell: VS colours its control words as keywords, not control flow
PowerShell: VS leaves cmdlet names plain
PowerShell: VS draws type literals ([string]) in its comment green, in both themes (sampled)
JS/TS: VS colours every identifier that is not a type or function as a variable — properties, enum members and constants too, unlike C#
JS/TS: the class after new is a type in VS (the grammar scopes it as a function call)
JS/TS: VS draws interfaces, enums, primitive types and this-as-a-type in the type colour
JS/TS: a regular expression is one string colour in VS, quantifiers and classes included
JS/TS: JSDoc text is plain comment green, tags keywords, parameter names variables, types plain
Markdown inline code (keyword blue in VS, sampled)
